settings.name_in_paper: Quantum non-linear bandit optimization (bounded value quantum bandit setting) with realizable parametric function class
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Quantum oracle access: each action is associated with a quantum sampling oracle and the learner uses quantum Monte Carlo mean estimation.
unmapped: Feedback is via a quantum sampling oracle O_x encoding the reward distribution (quantum Monte Carlo mean estimation), not classical samples
Black-box objective over arbitrary domain X subset R^{d_x}, approximated by a realizable parametric class f_w with w in [0,1]^{d_w}, bounded value/gradient/Hessian (C_f, C_g, C_h)
Learner knows constants C_g, C_h, C_0 used in confidence radius beta_s
settings.definition_quote: in (bounded value) quantum bandit setting, after taking the same action $\vx_t$ multiple times, the function oracle returns $y_t$ that satisfies $|y_t - f_0(\vx_t)| \leq \epsilon_t$ ... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T f_0(\vx^*) - f_0(\vx_t)$

symbols.d_w: dimension of the parameter space of the parametric function class f_w

conditions: Assumption 2: realizable parametric class, f_0 = f_{w*}, W subset [0,1]^{d_w}
Assumption 4: expected loss satisfies (tau,gamma)-growth or mu-local strong convexity at w*, with c-local self-concordance
existence of a quantum non-linear regression oracle (Theorem 9)
tuning: QME_1 with accuracy eps_s and failure delta/m

source.label: thm:cr
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 2, 3, and 4 hold. There is an absolute value $C$ such that after $\tilde{O}(T_0)$ iterations in Step 1 of Algorithm 1 where $T_0$ satisfies $T^2_0 \geq C d_\vw \iota \max\{...\}$ ... Then Algorithm 1 with parameters $T_0=\sqrt{T}, \lambda=T$ satisfies that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_T = O\big(d_w^2 \log^\frac{3}{2}(T) \log (d_w \log (T))\big)$.

results.notes: Quantum setting (out of scope). Noise mapped to bounded_01 since QME_1 (bounded value [0,1]) is used; paper notes QME_2 (bounded variance) also works. Restated as Theorem 31 in appendix. Hidden dependence on delta and constants absorbed in O.
